children: Comex copper futures fell more than 9% this week, their steepest weekly decline of 2026, as hedge funds cut bullish positions. Eleven of the biggest copper miners lost about $127 billion in market value, according to BeInCrypto. Copper had reached a record in September on expectations of rising demand from AI data centers, but by Friday it had fallen to about $5.46 per pound, its lowest level since March. Hedge funds and other large speculators’ net bullish position declined from more than 80,000 contracts in late September to about 28,700 by November 17; speculative investors sold $1.3 billion in Comex copper futures in the week ending November 10, their seventh consecutive weekly sale. Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller said on November 17 that he was short copper. Analysts differ on the drivers, citing either an overstated AI premium or hotter-than-expected October inflation, higher rate expectations and a stronger dollar. Meanwhile, Chinese importers are paying record premiums, and traders have booked shipments from the U.S. to China. The International Energy Agency forecasts a possible 25% shortfall in mined copper by 2035. Copper fell below $5.63, a support level cited by Saxo Bank’s Ole Hansen, whose next level is $5.32. Saxo says reduced fund positioning may leave the market less exposed to further selling; the next CFTC report will show whether hedge funds continued to cut bets.

title: Copper Posts Its Worst Week of 2026 as Funds Cut Bets
